title: The wash-n-dry
subtitle: Fulton Street · Thursday afternoon
alt: A narrow, grimy 1970s laundromat with washers on the left, a folding table and stacked dryers on the right, and a green street door at the far end.
summary: A working neighbourhood laundromat, not a polished period set. Chipped enamel, stained linoleum and tired green paint make the place feel used every day.
design: Flat fluorescent light inside; pale, dirty daylight through the windows. Keep the composition horizontal and grounded at human height.
continuity: The screenplay specifies six washers; the sixth clanks. This selected master is a mood and layout reference, not an exact machine count.

title: The threshold
subtitle: Sunny's Wash-n-Dry · Brooklyn, 1975
alt: The weathered green storefront of Sunny's Wash-n-Dry, with its street door open and washers visible through a dirty window.
summary: A battered green storefront on a lived-in Brooklyn block. Sunlight at the open door contrasts with the sickly fluorescent interior.
design: The doorway connects the room to the unseen street. Keep the offscreen exchange outside; the man is not identified in this scene.
continuity: Peanut pushes through the propped door. On his laugh, glimpse only a cigarette cherry and a gold pinky ring, not a face.

title: Table continuity
subtitle: Towels, newspaper and two quarters
alt: A laundromat folding table at right with one stack of folded pale towels at the back and a single newspaper toward the front.
summary: Keep one neat stack of off-white towels at the back-right of the folding table and one newspaper toward the front until Peanut picks it up.
design: The battered table stays in place across the brothers' coverage. Preserve the stained surfaces and the washer-left / table-right geography.
continuity: Peanut reads the Daily News, then slaps two quarters on the machine. The voted quarters still places them on the table; use the screenplay's blocking for the final shot.

title: Bug's recorder
subtitle: One recorder · one wired microphone
alt: An isolated beige-grey shoebox cassette recorder with its complete wired handheld microphone and coiled cable, on a transparent background.
summary: A compact beige-grey shoebox cassette recorder with visible tape transport and meter. The complete handheld microphone remains connected by its cable.
design: Place the recorder beside Bug on a washer. One recorder, one microphone: no added radio or boombox. The reference PNG has genuine transparency.
continuity: Bug records the washer, returns and labels the cassette DRYER BEAT. Later he makes the beat by physically splicing tape, not with a sampler.
